source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a planet's temperature can be predicted from distance from the Sun alone.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Sun is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use distance from the Sun as a starting expectation, not as the only rule.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: planet temperature happens first, and that produces distance from the Sun plus atmospheric heat trapping.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Use distance from the Sun as a starting expectation, not as the only rule is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Planets closer to the Sun generally receive more heat, but a thick atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide can trap heat strongly, so Venus is the hottest planet even though it is not closest to the Sun. distance from the Sun plus atmospheric heat trapping -> planet temperature The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Planets closer to the Sun generally receive more heat, but a thick atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide can trap heat strongly, so Venus is the hottest planet even though it is not closest to the Sun. The closest planet to the Sun must always be the hottest planet.
